title: Choose BayuPandu's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Launch Task Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Sketches are the real 240×320 main flight screen.

options.label: Launch Task Board
options.lineage: the whiteboard at take-off where the day's task, turnpoints and weather are briefed in marker
options.thesis: The flight written up like the launch briefing board: black marker figures on white, ruled lines, a running thermal log.
options.viewport: Climb rate huge at top with sign and side of a centre rule; altitude and L/D on ruled rows; the last three thermals written as board lines below.
options.risk: A light ground glares on a cheap transmissive TFT at low backlight; it pays off on transflective/MIP panels.

raised.raise: Destructive actions (end flight, stop log) stand alone and need a long press, never next to a page key.
One figure owns each page; on Flight that is climb, at twice the size of anything else.
UP/DOWN snap between complete pages; nothing scrolls, nothing is half-shown.
Every state is a written mark: stale values struck through, estimates bracketed, so nothing relies on colour.
Hierarchy by size alone: three type sizes, one weight family, no boxes or cards.

options.label: Direction Sign
options.lineage: Indonesian green highway direction signs and yellow warning signs
options.thesis: Read at speed, in sun, in one glance: every figure set like a road sign legend.
options.viewport: A green sign panel with climb as a big arrow legend; altitude and L/D as distance-style lines; warnings swap to yellow diamond panels.
options.risk: Familiar sign language; green ground competes with any green-for-lift habit pilots carry from other varios.

options.label: Jet-Age Ticket Wallet
options.lineage: carbon-copy airline coupons and baggage stubs
options.thesis: Each glide and thermal is a coupon; stale data gets stamped VOID instead of disappearing.
options.viewport: A coupon head with climb in carbon numerals; the current glide as a torn stub below with GS and L/D boxes.
options.case: Holds product clarity (legs and VOID states fit XC well) but pilots don't identify with airline paperwork.
options.risk: Ruled boxes multiply and drift towards the busy screen you ruled out.

options.label: Dark Developer Console
options.case: Loses both: pilots aren't developers, and graphite with hairlines dies in sun.
options.kept: Destructive actions isolated and deliberately gated.

options.label: Zoo Guide Map
options.case: Loses both: playful lobes blur figures pilots must read instantly.

options.label: Vertical Video Feed
options.thesis: One item fills the screen; the next is one snap away.
options.case: Loses both: it is a phone app, which you ruled out.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference Setting
options.thesis: Two text columns around a rail of keys.
options.case: Loses both: a reading layout on a glance instrument.
options.kept: States as printed marks: struck, bracketed, filled.

options.label: Variable Font Specimen
options.case: Loses both: nothing to do with flying.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What XC varios ship: a grid of labelled data boxes with a vario bar down the side, done cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Vario bar on the left edge; six equal boxes: climb, altitude, GS, L/D, avg, flight time.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every Flymaster/XCTrack-style layout, and the generic box grid you ruled out.
